question: A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of painful swelling on the right side of her face. The pain worsens when she eats. Examination of the face shows a right-sided, firm swelling that is tender to palpation. Oral examination shows no abnormalities. Ultrasonography shows a stone located in a duct that runs anterior to the masseter muscle and passes through the buccinator muscle. Sialoendoscopy is performed to remove the stone. At which of the following sites is the endoscope most likely to be inserted during the procedure?

options.opa: Lateral to the superior labial frenulum
options.opc: Lateral to the second upper molar tooth
options.opd: Into the floor of the mouth

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Stone in duct anterior to masseter muscle -> Sialoendoscopy performed to remove stone -> Endoscope inserted lateral to the lingual frenulum -> 80% CHAIN: Painful swelling on right side of face worsens with eating -> Stone located in duct anterior to masseter muscle -> Sialoendoscopy performed to remove stone -> Endoscope inserted lateral to the lingual frenulum -> 75% CHAIN: Ultrasonography shows stone in duct anterior to masseter muscle -> Sialoendoscopy performed to remove stone -> Endoscope inserted lateral to the lingual frenulum -> 80%
analysis: Based on the description of the stone located in a duct that runs anterior to the masseter muscle and passes through the buccinator muscle, the most likely site for the endoscope to be inserted during the sialoendoscopy procedure is lateral to the lingual frenulum.
